test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - Reasoning (Held on: 20 Nov, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: reasoning
question:
Two statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some camels are donkeys.

Some donkeys are cows.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some cows are camels.

II. Some donkeys are camels.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows

solution:
Statements:

Some camels are donkeys.

Some donkeys are cows.

The least possible Venn diagram is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a0393b00c1e3b44f1e9e19f5b9eba7cb9a8ec3e5f4d0c109e9523e1ac6b23257.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some cows are camels. - **False **(because there is no direct relation between cows and camels. So, it can be possible but not definite)

II. Some donkeys are camels. - **True **(because Some camels are donkeys. So, Some donkeys are camels too)

Hence, the correct answer is "Only conclusions II follow".
